title: Virtual Head Attention: Cracking LLM Memory

beats.text: Standard attention forces a brutal trade-off: shrink the cache and lose intelligence, or expand it and kill your GPU throughput.
beats.visual_focus: A scale tipping violently between a brain icon and a server rack icon.

beats.text: Virtual Head Attention shatters this by using two linear operations: Q-Premix and Postmix to simulate head diversity without physical overhead.
beats.visual_focus: Geometric lines folding into a single, clean, high-density vector path.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—'choking on their own memory' is a relatable pain point for anyone who's tried to run a local LLM. I didn't swipe because you got straight to the point. However, when you mentioned 'Q-Premix and Postmix,' I had to pause to think if those were standard architectural terms or specific to this paper. It's a bit jargon-heavy, but since you explained the 'folding into weights' part immediately after, I stayed with you.

Why is Virtual Head Attention a major breakthrough? Because the design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality.

Everyone thought standard methods were enough, until Virtual Head Attention proved: gQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute.
